rounds.text: Loyal Textile Mills is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.55x [E1, E52]. While the market remains fixated on historical struggles, the company is demonstrating a clear operational turnaround, evidenced by a 60% growth in compounded profit over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a 101% year-over-year increase in net profit [E58]. This momentum is supported by a sector-wide tailwind [E64, E66] and recent quarterly improvements, where operating margins expanded by 5 percentage points compared to the year-ago quarter [E27]. Furthermore, the company has successfully begun deleveraging, with borrowings reduced to Rs 207 Cr from Rs 216 Cr [E35, E51], while simultaneously generating substantial free cash flow of Rs 229 Cr [E32]. The stock’s technical position, currently trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, suggests that the market is beginning to recognize this shift in fundamentals [E42]. Conceded: the company faces significant challenges including negative ROE [E8, E12], a lack of dividend payments [E3], and a history of declining sales growth [E13, E14, E15, E16].

Loyal Textile Mills faces a structural decline characterized by a consistent erosion of its top line, with compounded sales growth plummeting by 33% over the last three years and 32% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E16]. This chronic inability to generate revenue is compounded by severe operational inefficiency, evidenced by a negative return on equity of -25.8% and a negative return on assets of -7.12% [E7, E12]. The company’s balance sheet is precarious, as debt now exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.02x, while current liabilities outstrip current assets at a ratio of 0.85x [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the firm suffers from a low interest coverage ratio and an extreme EV/EBITDA valuation of 139.75x, which sits far above the sector benchmark of 8.89x [E10, E53]. Investors face significant volatility, as evidenced by an annualized volatility of 52.9% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -82.1% [E45, E46]. Conceded: the company has reduced its total borrowings to Rs 207 Cr [E35] and is currently trading at a discount to book value [E1, E52]. Despite these minor balance sheet improvements, the long-term trend of negative compounded share price growth remains a stark warning of persistent value destruction [E18, E19, E20].

The bear flags revenue contraction [E15, E16], but ignores that the company is experiencing a powerful operational turnaround where profit growth over the trailing twelve months has surged by 60% [E17] and net profit is up 101% year-on-year [E58]. Conceded: return metrics are currently negative [E7, E12], but this sentiment is stale because results are actively accelerating with a rules-based score of 63 out of 100 [E57, E65] and quarterly operating margins have jumped by 5 percentage points to 2% [E27]. The bear attacks the balance sheet leverage [E33, E34], but overlooks the active deleveraging where borrowings have been successfully reduced to Rs 207 Cr [E35, E51] alongside a massive free cash flow of Rs 229 Cr [E32]. Conceded: the EV/EBITDA is high [E10], yet the stock trades at an ultra-deep discount at 0.55x book value [E1] while sitting above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E42]. Finally, the bear warns of a long-term downtrend [E18, E19, E20], but recent price momentum is validated by a supportive textile sector tailwind score of +0.60 [E66] where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 54% [E49].

The bull points to TTM profit growth of 60% [E17] and a 101% YoY net profit surge [E58], but this comes on the back of multi-year top-line destruction where compounded sales growth over 3 years is -33% [E15] and TTM sales growth is -32% [E16], compounded by an admission that earnings are inflated by Rs 11.6 Cr in other income [E56]. Conceded: quarterly operating margins improved by 5 percentage points to 2% [E27], but the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends remain classified as inconsistent [E28, E29] and the company's operating margin remains in negative territory at -3% [E26]. While the bull highlights active debt reduction to Rs 207 Cr [E35, E51], it glosses over the severe structural risk that debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.02x [E33] and current liabilities exceeding current assets at a current ratio of 0.85x [E34]. Conceded: the stock trades at 0.55x book value [E1], yet this low valuation is entirely justified by a devastating ROE of -25.8% [E12], a median 3-year ROE of -25% [E24], and an extremely bloated EV/EBITDA of 139.75x compared to the sector benchmark of 8.89x [E10]. Finally, the bull leans on sector tailwinds [E66] and moving averages [E42], ignoring that the stock carries a staggering annualised volatility of 52.9% [E46], a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.39 [E47], and a brutal historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -82.1% [E45].
